_comment: Phase 3 (docs/platform-closure-plan.md) Step 1 inventory. Read-only audit, verified against main be70ba9 (VERSION 15.377), not carried forward from docs/reports/replication-readiness.md's prose without re-checking. Regenerate the summary counts with `npm run audit:replication -- --json`; this file adds the per-entrypoint detail that tool does not attempt (implicit read/write, unknown/no-module behavior, required change, regression risk, fixture/Yoma proof requirements) and one blocker class the tool's scan globs miss entirely (JSON config data).

auditToolCounts.note: docs/reports/replication-readiness.md's table (7 files) predates scripts/generate_argument_taxonomy.py's addition during Phase 2A; the live count is 8, not 7. scripts/audit_replication_readiness.py's SCAN_GLOBS also do not include *.json, so it does not see the config-data blocker (entry 9 below) at all.

blockers.entrypoint: scripts/worker_pipeline.py (13 subcommands: manifest, preflight, packet, prompt, scope, verify, review, queue, capability-scan, schema-matrix, docs, report, ci-check)
blockers.purpose: The entire worker pipeline: generates and validates worker manifests, runs preflight checks, builds work packets and prompts for bounded Rashi/structural/docs tasks, enforces file/JSON-path scope, verifies a completed pass (offline gates + build + tests), tracks queue progress, and regenerates reference docs.
blockers.currentModuleSelectionMechanism: argparse --module flag, default 'yoma', threaded into the generated manifest's 'module' field only. Never used to derive a filesystem path.
blockers.hardcodedAssumption: Lines 40-41: YROOT = REPO/'modules'/'yoma', YSCRIPTS = YROOT/'scripts', both module-blind constants. ~28 further literal 'modules/yoma/...' path prefixes across scope checks, freshness checks, content-path classification, and generated-file expectations (verified: 28 raw regex hits via audit_replication_readiness.py's PIN_RE/ID_RE on this file at be70ba9).
validatorsInvoked: validate_rashi_content.py, validate_rashi_repetition.py, validate_literal.py (all run with cwd=YROOT)
blockers.unknownModuleBehavior: Silently accepted. Manifest's 'module' field is set to the unknown string, but every allowedFiles entry, scope check, and generation command still literally names modules/yoma. Live-verified: `worker_pipeline.py manifest --type rashi-repair --module bogus-module --range 2a` produces a manifest with module='bogus-module' and allowedFiles=['modules/yoma/assets/learning/yoma/<daf>.learning.json', ...] - scope gates would pass while pointing at the wrong module, exactly as docs/reports/replication-readiness.md predicted.
blockers.noModuleBehavior: Defaults to 'yoma' silently (argparse default), no warning.
blockers.requiredChange: Thread the module id through a resolver into YROOT/YSCRIPTS and every derived path; move the ~28 literal prefixes to resolver-derived paths; reject an unresolvable module before any filesystem operation.
blockers.regressionRisk: High blast radius (every worker command) but mechanical: Yoma's own manifests must resolve identically once module=yoma is explicit instead of implicit. Primary risk is missing one of the ~28 call sites.
blockers.fixtureProofRequired: A fixture-targeted manifest of every task type must resolve fixture paths only, reject Yoma targets, and worker:verify must pass against the fixture module end to end.
blockers.yomaProofRequired: Every existing Yoma manifest/preflight/packet/prompt/verify/queue/docs command must produce byte-identical output with module=yoma explicit vs. today's implicit default.

blockers.purpose: Unit tests for worker_pipeline.py's scope/policy enforcement (allowedFiles resolution, forbidden-file rejection, structure policy, allowlist policy).
blockers.currentModuleSelectionMechanism: None; tests hardcode Yoma fixture paths directly.
blockers.hardcodedAssumption: 32 literal 'modules/yoma/...' path references (e.g. 'modules/yoma/MODULE.md', 'modules/yoma/assets/learning/yoma/2a.learning.json') used as both input fixtures and expected-output assertions.
inputPaths: in-test literal path strings only; no real filesystem fixture module
validatorsInvoked: worker_pipeline.py's own scope-check functions, imported directly
blockers.unknownModuleBehavior: n/a - tests do not exercise module selection, only path-scope logic against hardcoded Yoma-shaped strings
blockers.requiredChange: Once worker_pipeline.py's scope functions accept a resolved module, add parallel test cases using the fixture module's paths so scope logic is proven module-generic, not just proven correct for one hardcoded shape.
blockers.regressionRisk: Low - purely additive; existing Yoma-path assertions stay as regression tests for the Yoma module specifically.
blockers.fixtureProofRequired: New test cases proving scope resolution for the fixture module id.
blockers.yomaProofRequired: All existing 32 Yoma-path assertions continue to pass unchanged.

blockers.purpose: Audits whether the linked Rashi renderer is ready across every daf (used to gate the legacy-renderer retirement and ongoing readiness checks).
blockers.hardcodedAssumption: Line 52: const YOMA = resolve(ROOT, 'modules/yoma'); plus doc-comment references to modules/yoma/scripts/allowlists/*.json (5 total mentions).
outputPaths: stdout report; readiness JSON consumed by the sharded browser workflow
validatorsInvoked: audit_rashi_association.py indirectly via the sharded browser run
blockers.unknownModuleBehavior: No module parameter exists; always resolves Yoma regardless of any caller intent.
blockers.requiredChange: Accept a module id, resolve YOMA-equivalent root through the shared resolver.
blockers.regressionRisk: Low - single constant substitution plus path derivation.
blockers.fixtureProofRequired: Readiness audit runs against the fixture's own (declared-enabled) Rashi allowlists and reports correctly, or reports 'Rashi disabled' cleanly when the fixture disables the feature.
blockers.yomaProofRequired: Identical readiness report for Yoma before/after.

blockers.purpose: Verifies a sharded browser-test run's evidence artifact (per-shard union equals the authoritative daf list, ci=true, correct commit).
blockers.requiredChange: Accept a module id or an explicit artifact-path override derived from the resolver; keep the default aimed at Yoma only through an explicit alias.
blockers.fixtureProofRequired: Can verify a fixture-scoped shard artifact without touching modules/yoma/scripts/allowlists/rashi_browser_shard_result.json.
blockers.yomaProofRequired: Identical verification behavior for the existing Yoma artifact path.

blockers.purpose: Runs audit_rashi_association.py --json once and writes its result for CI/local use.
outputPaths: JSON result to the path the caller specifies
blockers.requiredChange: Accept a module id, resolve the module's own association-audit script path (a per-module script by convention, so this becomes 'resolve modules/<id>/scripts/audit_rashi_association.py' or fail if the module disables the Rashi feature).
blockers.fixtureProofRequired: Runs against the fixture's own association audit when Rashi is enabled; fails clearly (not silently) if the fixture disables Rashi and this is invoked anyway.

blockers.purpose: Combines per-shard sharded browser-test results into one artifact.
blockers.hardcodedAssumption: auditScript resolves modules/yoma/scripts/audit_rashi_association.py (1 mention, for the authoritative daf list used to verify shard union completeness).
blockers.requiredChange: Same as entry 5 - resolve the module's own script path via the module id.
blockers.fixtureProofRequired: Combines fixture shard results using the fixture's own daf list.
blockers.yomaProofRequired: Identical combination result for Yoma's shards.

blockers.purpose: Runs one shard of the sharded Rashi-association browser workflow.
blockers.fixtureProofRequired: Runs one shard against the fixture's (small) daf list correctly, including the single-shard case.
blockers.yomaProofRequired: Identical per-shard results for Yoma's 8-shard run.

blockers.purpose: Generates the app.jsx-embedded argumentFlow category-registry block from shared/argument_step_taxonomy.json and checks its freshness (Phase 2A's category-coverage mechanism).
blockers.hardcodedAssumption: 1 mention: reads modules/yoma/learning_data.js to enumerate every observed argumentFlow.type value across the corpus being registered.
blockers.requiredChange: Accept a module id (or a list) and enumerate observed type values across every selected module's learning_data.js, so a fixture module's own argumentFlow types are covered by the same registry mechanism without being conflated with Yoma's.
blockers.regressionRisk: Medium - this generates a block embedded in app.jsx, a file shared across all modules; must not regress Yoma's already-100%-covered category rendering.
blockers.fixtureProofRequired: Fixture's argumentFlow type values are represented in the registry (or the fixture's own types are already in the canonical 13, proving no gap) without altering Yoma's registry entries.
blockers.yomaProofRequired: app.jsx's generated registry block is byte-identical for Yoma's existing 119 type values before/after; validate_argument_taxonomy.py stays green.
blockers.note: This blocker is not in docs/reports/replication-readiness.md's original 7-file table. It was added by Phase 2A after that table was last written, and the existing audit tool's mention-scan (scripts/audit_replication_readiness.py) already catches it under scripts/*.py - the live count is 8 PINNED files, not 7, confirmed by re-running `npm run audit:replication -- --json` against be70ba9.

blockers.entrypoint: scripts/worker_task_types.json (registry) and its ~13 per-type allowedFiles/allowedJsonPaths declarations
blockers.purpose: Declares every worker task type's scope contract - which files and JSON paths a bounded worker manifest of that type may touch. Consumed by worker_pipeline.py's scope, verify, docs, and schema-matrix commands.
blockers.currentModuleSelectionMechanism: None; every entry's allowedFiles/forbiddenFiles/generationCommands/buildTestCommands hardcodes literal modules/yoma/... strings.
blockers.hardcodedAssumption: 116 literal 'modules/yoma' occurrences across the registry (grep-counted at be70ba9). This is a config-data blocker, not a code blocker, and it is NOT caught by scripts/audit_replication_readiness.py, whose SCAN_GLOBS only cover *.py/*.mjs/*.js/*.yml files - it never scans *.json. This is a gap in the existing audit tool, discovered during this Step 1 verification, not merely a restatement of the prior 7-file table.
outputPaths: docs/reports/task-type-reference.md, docs/reports/schema-coverage-matrix.md (both generated from this registry)
validatorsInvoked: worker_pipeline.py cmd_schema_matrix cross-checks this registry against scripts/worker_schema_scope.json (which is already module-agnostic, 0 modules/yoma mentions)
blockers.unknownModuleBehavior: The registry itself has no module concept; every type's paths are Yoma paths regardless of what module a manifest claims.
blockers.requiredChange: Either template the module-specific path fragments (substituting a resolved module id at manifest-generation time, the way <daf> is already substituted) or restructure allowedFiles to be module-relative and resolved against the requested module by worker_pipeline.py, never read as literal absolute-from-Yoma strings.
blockers.regressionRisk: High if mishandled - this is the actual security/scope boundary the whole worker pipeline depends on; must not create a path where a fixture-targeted manifest's allowedFiles accidentally still resolves a Yoma path, or vice versa.
blockers.fixtureProofRequired: Every task type's allowedFiles resolves to fixture paths only when the manifest's module is the fixture; a mismatched module+path combination is rejected (this is explicitly required by the Phase 3 acceptance criteria: 'reject a manifest whose module and paths disagree').
blockers.yomaProofRequired: Every existing Yoma task type continues to resolve exactly its current allowedFiles list for module=yoma; scripts/worker:schema-matrix and worker:docs regenerate byte-identical output.

alreadyGeneric.evidence: dataScriptPattern /^modules\/[a-z0-9_-]+\/learning_data\.js$/ accepts any module id shape, rejects uppercase and traversal; live-tested by audit_replication_readiness.py's fixture_check(), all pass.
isAllowedModuleDataScript enforces the matching runtime allowlist; ?module= is read and an unknown id falls back to the landing page, not to Yoma content.
MYSUGYA_MANIFEST is an array registry, not a single Yoma entry.
0 modules/yoma mentions; module selection happens inside individual specs, not the runner config.
0 modules/yoma mentions; already a JSON-path-only classification with no filesystem prefixes.
0 modules/yoma mentions in workflow YAML itself; Yoma selection happens through the npm scripts and .mjs tools these workflows call, which are covered by the blocker entries above.

cloneCostNotBlocking.note: These are the cost of cloning modules/yoma/scripts/ for a second module (each of the 31 files names its own module id in a per-module script; 46 :yoma-suffixed npm scripts would need :  <newid> siblings). Not a Phase 3 blocker under the stated acceptance criteria - Phase 3 requires generic commands to work correctly when given an explicit module, not that per-module script duplication be eliminated. Left as documented future work, not addressed by this campaign; a MODULE_ID-constant pattern (per docs/reports/replication-readiness.md) would reduce it but is optional.
